newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Hoogovens, unions meet to avert strike.
newsitem.headline: Hoogovens, unions meet to avert strike.

text.p: Trade unions and management at Dutch steel and aluminium maker Hoogovens said on Monday they would hold more talks on Tuesday in bid to agree on the company's restructuring plans and avert a potential strike.
Unions said negotiations broke down at the end of January over Hoogovens' programme to redeploy and discharge around 3,000 employees and recruit 1,000 young, highly trained workers.

"We will open new negotiations with management tomorrow but the ultimatim still stands that if we have no agreement by the 13th (Thursday), then we will ballot our members on strike action," a spokesman told Reuters.

A Hoogovens spokesman said the talks would be held tomorrow at the request of the unions and he confirmed the dispute only concerned the company's steel division. Any strike action would leave aluminium production facilities unaffected, he said.

Unions said that while they did not object to some reduction in the workforce, they were opposed to forcing employees to re-locate to company divisions in other parts of the country and any compulsory redundancies.
The company was confident a strike could be avoided.
"We are always optimistic we can reach an agreement," the Hoogovens spokesman said.
